venue.name: The Whale Interpretive Centre
venue.description: The Whale Interpretive Centre sits at the end of the Telegraph Cove boardwalk on northern Vancouver Island, with its entrance facing Johnstone Strait. It opened in 2002 and is run by the Johnstone Strait Killer Whale Interpretive Centre Society, a registered charity established in 1993, with a mission to increase public awareness about the biology of marine mammals and the threats facing their populations. A fire on the Telegraph Cove boardwalk on December 31, 2024 destroyed the building and its entire collection, and the centre reopened to the public on August 1, 2026 with three skeletons that were off site at the time, a Dall's porpoise, a Risso's dolphin and the only pygmy sperm whale ever recorded in British Columbia, along with specimens donated by the public. Admission is by donation for the 2026 season, the interior is still undergoing improvements, and the society expects construction to be fully finished by summer 2027.
venue.hours_notes: 9:30 AM to 5:30 PM, 7 days a week. Closed Sunday, September 20, 2026 for a scheduled power outage, reopening Monday, September 21, 2026.
venue.seasonal_notes: The Whale Interpretive Centre reopened to the public on Saturday, August 1, 2026, after the December 31, 2024 boardwalk fire. Admission is by donation for the 2026 season. The exterior of the building is finished and the interior is still undergoing improvements; the society anticipates that construction will be fully finished by summer 2027. The site does not publish a closing date for the season.

programs.name: Visit the Whale Interpretive Centre
programs.description: The centre is open to the public 9:30 AM to 5:30 PM, 7 days a week, and admission is by donation for the 2026 season. The inside is still undergoing improvements and is not quite finished, and staff are there to greet visitors and share information about the marine mammals of the area. The site publishes no group rate, no group booking route, no minimum age and no capacity limit.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the Telegraph Cove boardwalk to the building at the far end, whose entrance faces Johnstone Strait, then go inside to look at marine mammal skeletons and specimens, including a Dall's porpoise, a Risso's dolphin and the only pygmy sperm whale ever recorded in British Columbia. Staff are on hand to talk about the whales, dolphins and porpoises of the area and to answer questions.
programs.our_note: The centre reopened in August 2026 after the boardwalk fire and the inside is still being finished, so expect a smaller collection than the photographs on the site show. Nothing about washrooms, somewhere to eat or getting a stroller in is published anywhere, so ask when you call.
programs.practical_summary: The visit is indoors at the end of the Telegraph Cove boardwalk, open seven days a week from 9:30 to 5:30, and admission is by donation. Washrooms, a place to eat, wheelchair and stroller access and parking for a bus are not stated anywhere on the site, so it is worth a call first.
programs.extra_fees_note: Admission is by donation for the 2026 season. The site does not name a suggested amount for general admission.
programs.evidence: Admission to the Whale Interpretive Centre is by donation for the 2026 season.

programs.name: Guided tour or marine mammal presentation
programs.description: Guided tours of the collection or presentations on marine mammals are offered throughout the season and are scheduled in advance by calling 250-949-1143. Tours and presentations are by donation, with $8.00 per person suggested. The site does not say how long a tour or presentation runs, how many people can come, what ages it suits, or how much notice is needed.
programs.what_children_do: Follow a staff member around the collection while they explain the skeletons and the animals they came from, or sit and listen to a presentation about marine mammals.
programs.our_note: Ring ahead if you want a tour or a talk, since both are arranged on the phone rather than online. How long they run, how many children can come and what ages they suit are not published, so settle all of that on the same call.
programs.practical_summary: Tours and presentations run through the season, are arranged by phone and are by donation with $8.00 per person suggested. The length, the group size and the ages they are pitched at are not published, so ask when you call.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $8.00 is a suggested donation per person rather than a set fee, and the site does not say whether children pay it.
programs.evidence: Tours and presentations are by donation; $8.00 per person is suggested.
